candidate.mistake_reason: Proposed a plan that depended on manually downloading a CSV from Google Finance and assuming a local file path without ensuring the file existed or providing a viable way to obtain it (Google Finance does not offer a direct CSV export).
candidate.first_mistake: This initial flawed assumption set up all subsequent steps to fail with missing-file errors and no alternative data acquisition method.
candidate.mistake_not_corrected: Later agents repeatedly retried the same approach and asked for the CSV but never obtained the data or changed the method (e.g., scraping or using an available source), so the core issue was never resolved.

confidences.reason: The log shows that the plan to download a CSV and use a local file path came from the manager’s provided plan, not from the FinancialData_Expert’s own proposal at Step 0. At Step 0, the agent was instructed to follow that plan and did not introduce the CSV dependency themselves. While it’s true Google Finance doesn’t provide a direct CSV export, attributing that planning mistake to Step 0 is inaccurate based on the log.

The earliest concrete error in the log is the IndentationError at Step 1, not an assumption made at Step 0. Step 0 outlined a plan but did not execute anything that directly caused the failure. The missing-file issue did contribute to later failures, but it was not the first mistake; the first was the code indentation error.

Throughout the log, agents kept rerunning code expecting a local CSV and repeatedly hit FileNotFoundError. They only advised manual download and did not obtain the data themselves or switch to an alternative method (e.g., scraping or another data source). The final attempt merely searched and returned the Google Finance page link without retrieving data or updating the approach. Thus, the core issue was never resolved.
